The test image shows a tomato plant with:
- Severely wilted, brown/dead leaves
- A stem with visible decay and a dark lesion/canker
- Overall plant collapse
- Black plastic mulch/greenhouse setting

Top candidates: Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot, Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers, Southern_Blight, Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato

Now I'll view one reference image per class before revisiting.

I've now used all 16 reference image views. Let me summarize my analysis:

**Test image features:**
- Tomato plant with severe wilting/complete death of all leaves (brown, desiccated)
- Stem has a prominent dark/blackened lesion at a specific point
- Stem appears brownish-gray, bleached/discolored, dried
- Greenhouse setting: black plastic mulch, wire trellis
- Girdling pattern — plant appears to have died above the stem lesion

**Reference comparisons:**
- **Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot (Bugwood_2):** Most visually similar — wilted/dead plant on wire trellis with black plastic mulch in greenhouse setting, identical context; plant dead on one side with remaining green
- **Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers (Bugwood_7):** Stem with dark canker area — stem lesion pattern similar, but less severe overall collapse
- **Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato (Bugwood_18):** Shows stem canker and wilted leaves in background — partial match
- All other classes showed microscopy, lab specimens, leaf-pattern diseases, or clearly different field presentations

**Decision:** The Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot (Bugwood_2) reference matched best — same greenhouse/trellis/black-plastic setting, similar full-plant collapse. The bleached stem with a specific rot point causing complete plant death above it is consistent with Sclerotinia timber rot (which girdles the stem).
